newsitem.title: UK: Abbey National extends post-results gain.
newsitem.headline: Abbey National extends post-results gain.

text.p: Shares in Abbey National Plc rose in early trade on Wednesday, extending gains after results which showed growth in businesses outside its non-core mortgage operations, dealers said.

The Financial Times Lex column said Abbey was achieving "impressive" gains in areas such as life assurance. It said the company should achieve earnings growth approaching ten percent and the stock was "reasonable value" since it was trading at a discount to rivals.

Abbey shares were up 12-1/2p or 1.5 percent at 858-1/2 by 0754 GMT and other banks also rose, with Lloyds TSB Plc up 10-1/2p at 670, Barclays Plc up 19p at 12.57-1/2 stg and National Westminster Bank Plc up 4p at 869. Royal Bank of Scotland Plc was up 10p at 640.
HSBC Holdings Plc was up 24p at 21.61 stg, also helped by gains in shares in Hong Kong where half its stock is owned.
Dealers noted that Abbey was due a bounce after underperforming other UK banks in recent weeks and that the whole sector continued to be underpinned by bid and merger speculation.

"Abbey shares were oversold and that's why there's been a bit of bounce," said Robert Law, analyst at Lehman Brothers. "The results have put the spotlight back on the sector, there had been some nervousness ahead of the figures which was not really justified."
Continuing the banks reporting season kicked off by Abbey, Lloyds reports first-half figures on Friday.
